name: Korinek et al. 2026, extreme-change scenario
description: Swaps korinek-2026.json from the substantial scenario to the EXTREME one: transformative AI, nearly half of today's cognitive work done by AI by 2030. Replaces the exogenous adoption curve (end point 0.45) and the two scenario-specific parameters (psi 0.9, re-employment 18 months). This is the scenario the reduced form is most strained by: it reproduces the published GDP boost to within 0.7pp and cognitive unemployment to within 0.7pp, inside tolerance but on a mechanism with none of the paper's structure behind it.

source.label: Korinek et al. 2026 reproduction, reduced form; see constants.ts KORINEK_SCENARIOS (extreme: psi = 0.9)
source.note: Fraction of AI-affected cognitive tasks automated rather than augmented, chosen per scenario so the displaced pool lands on the published cognitive-unemployment number.

source.label: Korinek et al. 2026 reproduction, reduced form; see constants.ts KORINEK_SCENARIOS (extreme: 18 months)
source.note: This repo's own displaced-pool residence time, not the paper's search discount mu.

source.label: Scenario input: share of US cognitive tasks performed by AI by end-2030 (0.45) (their m x d), ramped from 1% in mid-2026 along the logistic path in validation/korinek.ts::adoptionPath
source.note: Korinek et al. treat the capability/adoption path as an exogenous input and derive outcomes from it; this model does the same. The 2030 end point (0.118 substantial, 0.023 modest, 0.45 extreme) is from the paper's scenarios; the logistic shape between mid-2026 and end-2030 is this repo's own smoothing assumption, not the paper's.
